Pucker up, I thought i was only gonna talk some shit for a few sentences, but it ended up a whole fucking page. Well...if you ever wondered what an ultralight aluminium snub nosed revolver such as a S&W 642 feels like, here are my impressions.

People now days don't even consider snubby revolvers when looking into CC options. Now i have more insight into why. They kinda suck.

I figured, people just read that it's a 5 shot, and 1.4" thick, and say: "well a pocket auto is 6+1, and less then 1" thick, therefore it is better". But some guy on youtube was showing how despite the thickness, they actually conceal BETTER in pocket carry, because the thick cylinder lifts up the fabric, and breaks up the silhouette of the gun. So while you can certainly see there is something in the pocket, it looks nothing like a gun. Meanwhile, the thinner then 1" autoloader prints less, but when it does, its 100% clear that its a gun. Because its totally flat.

So ok, let me try one out. My previous experiences are shooting full sized, full weight, full grip .357 revolvers like S&W 686 for example. The sights were big and adjustable so they were on target. The double action pull, and the .357 would slow down your rate of fire quite a bit compared to an autoloader. But with .38 it was tame, and at leas it was dead accurate in single action. The model in question now was S&W 642. With a 2" barrel and an aluminium frame, it comes in at 14.4 oz / 408.2g. Now that's a carry peace! Fucking noice eh? But....

 

My main concern with these aluminium frame 2" snubbies was that almost all of them come with non adjustable sights, and usually don't have even a fiber optic front, let alone tritium. But S&W wouldn't build a gun that was way off would they? Well...they would. At 15m, with slow and meticulous fire in single action, the hits were off at least 5" to the right and 5" up. WTF? And i wasn't "doing it wrong" as the group itself was about 2", just completely displaced off the aiming point. The gun seemed to be relatively new and in great shape, so unless it was a lemon....

Now if i used a different bullet, that POI might have shifted more to the center, and it would be possible to file the front sight, but then you are locked in to that one ammo type. Its just a stupid and permanent way of doing it, as both sights are part of the frame and can't be replaced.

The second issue was that the sights themselves sucked. They were small, round, no tritium, no fiber optic, no paint..nothing. Aligning them and maintaining the picture was much harder. Sure, they need to be rounded so they don't snag on the pull out of the pocket, but that is no justification for making them suck in all other aspects. And this was a problem because..the recoil. I've read before on a lot of forums that they suck to shoot, as it's harsh as hell. I thought it might have been some soy milk involved since I've seen people bitch about a .357 being painful, but.....leme tell ya. It sucks. It felt like 4x more recoil than a full sized 9mm, even a polymer gun, while having half the kinetic energy from its 38 special round. It kicked more than .357mag out of a normal revolver such as a S&W 686.

The tiny grip is so well rounded and fits in your fist, that it's doesn't really cause pain, but its an annoying kind of sudden muzzle flip. A big .45 ACP gun may have recoil, but its a pleasurable recoil. It's more rearwards, and gradual. Its like a ship-side pirate cannon. A .45 is like squeezing a girls ass hard. An airweight snubby was like kicking her in the ass. Nether might cause actual pain, but one will be sexy, and the other annoying. Performance wise, that violent muzzle flip simply ruins your sight picture, and reacquiring it is slow due to the shitty sights.

 

So with all that in mind, i tried some rapid fire. "Wow i can't shoot this worth a shit!" Sure, i was able to stage the double action, and make a slow pull through the end, and do pretty well like that. But that's not panic mode rapid fire! When deliberately pulling fast, that thing was ALL OVER the place. The problem here was quad-fold. First the sights were way off and non adjustable, second the double action pull, third the massive muzzle flip, and fourth the re-acquisition of the tiny sights.

For reference, last time on the range i was deliberately testing accuracy with an improper press of a heavy double action trigger. I was shooting my CZ75 shadow in double action, as well as a 4.5" XD(m) with a typical mushy and long striker trigger. I would get a good grip, a perfect sight picture, then deliberately jerk the trigger as fast as possible, to simulate a panic reaction. With both guns, all that happened was that the shot group moved 2-3" to the left, while still maintaining good group size and vertical placement. Not the case with the airweight snubby.

For the last 3 shots out of the 50rnd box, i tried the same "ass pucker panic pull" test with rapid fire but one handed. I have no idea where those shots went, but they sure weren't on the silhouette. You could argue that "if you needed to shoot one handed, it would be point blank, and not 15m away". Sure, but its a fucking spear thrower that throws my spears 350 meters in one second. I DEMAND that it works at 15m with speed and precision regardless of conditions. Otherwise, i might as well carry a knife.

 

Granted, I'm comparing a full size autoloader to an ultra light aluminium compact revolver. And i have 10x more rounds through autoloaders than revolvers. But i never needed any real trigger time before i started to shoot an autoloader well. It was mostly discovering a few details about technique, such as the "thumbs over thumbs" grip, exerting sideways pressure on the frame, that counteracts the trigger jerk. Think about why is a rifle is more accurate to shoot. Because it has two points of stabilization. Add the stock, and now you have 3 points of stabilization. Well, the sideways pressure on the frame with the thumbs over thumbs grip gives the pistol a kind of two point stabilization deal. A revolver simply can't be held like that due to the cylinder and the cylinder gap blast. So even if it was an all steel, much heavier snubby i doubt it would have been much of an improvement in performance, while at the same time, the pocket gun factor would be ruined.

It is, and always will be, a performance hit compared to a well designed autoloader. Could i practice enough to learn to shoot it well? Sure, i could. But why would i? A small gun like that is not a range toy or a comp gun, where i can deliberately chose to do the harder thing as a personal challenge. It's a defensive tool for a kill of be killed scenario. The only thing that makes sense is to use whatever performs best, with 100% objectivity as judged by the target and the timer. If it also ends up fun and aesthetic, great, but it's not first priority. The only real advantage they have is that you can shoot them from within your pocket, while an autoloader instantly jams. And the revolver reliability is a meme. Yes they are not ammo sensitive, but when they do break, they lock up completely and you have nothing more than an paper weight. And modern ammo is great quality anyway.

TLDR: 14oz/400g pocket revolvers: no thank you, you kinda suck ass. You have shit sights, shit triggers, shit recoil, and I'll stick to autoloaders. If you are looking into these kind of guns, ABSOLUTELY try before you buy, for an entire box of ammo. I'm glad i did.

This is a Smith and Wesson Model 60. It's in my pocket right now.

It's all stainless steel. Weighs 22oz, 2 & 1/8" barrel, chambered in .357 magnum. It's ever so slightly longer than what you shot, but clearly much heavier. Also, notice the Delta Ergo grip l have on it.

The grip greatly helps with recoil. Won't fit everyone's hand, but made a huge improvement for mine. One of the biggest advantages with a revolver is complete control over grip size and shape.

Look at the front sight. I cut the ramp into a sharp angle so you can see it better. I also painted it bright orange. The rear sight has a corresponding orange, and they are sized so when they are lined up it is a single orange rectangle, but when misaligned there is a black break between them. I also painted the trough black.

As you said, these are designed so you find a load that is centered, then use it. Honestly, I'm just using FMJ .38 special. I'm looking for .38 wadcutters, too. Either has less recoil than .357, but still hurts. .357 out of a short barrel isn't the most efficient. I got this specifically because it's heavy and will give more controlability.

The trigger. It's heavy, by design. I smoothed the trigger internals with fine sandpaper and knife honing stones. That's just to reduce grittiness. Then you do lots of trigger pulls. Get some snap caps if you want. It's more difficult than a semi-auto, that's just how it is.

The hammer. I completely bobbed it. I also removed the single action sear. This is now double action only. "But clammy just get a Centennial". No. I put my thumb on the hammer when holstering. Added safety, you can't do that with an internal hammer. I much prefer hammer guns nowadays.

You already mentioned how it conceals well. This gun is also MUCH easier to yank out of your pocket. It's smooth and so angled in the back. My autoloaders do not come out as quickly, the back of the slide is just bulkier.

Daily Devotional

March 7

64 But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him. 65 And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it were given unto him of my Father. - John 6:64-65 (KJV)

What a shame it is, that there are many people in the church today that do not really believe in their hearts on Jesus. It is impossible for us to know just how many there are in our churches that are not believers, but Jesus taught that there would be many tares among the wheat (Matthew 13:24-30). We are not to try to weed them out of our churches, as we might also reject some that do believe. We are to just keep preaching the Gospel, and teaching God’s Word, and they will fall away on their own. When Jesus comes again, the Angels will go and pull out all those unbelievers out of the church (Matthew 13:41-42), so we need not worry about it. Many times our churches become like social clubs to attract more people, and that leads to many coming to church for the wrong reasons.

This is an awesome truth, that no one can come to Jesus except the Father draws him (John 6:44). This is why it is so very important that one accepts salvation when the Holy Spirit draws them, as if you don’t respond at that time, you may not ever get another chance. There is coming a time in your life, that the Holy Spirit will quit trying to draw you toward salvation (Genesis 6:3), so it is important that you not postpone your responding to His call. There are many that don’t recognize any of the benefits of walking with the Lord in this life, but think it only applies to the afterlife, and that is not so (John 10:10). Religion has been bad to not place any emphasis on the benefits that Christianity brings to our present life, making people think that it is not important to them now. We should teach the truth at all times – not just what people want to hear. Praise God for His Word!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
